# Monte

> Monte (https://monte.markets) is a free site for learning business statistics, one idea at a time. Fourteen topics from data and sampling to multiple regression, each with a plain explanation, a worked example, an interactive lab and timed drills. Games teach the same ideas with real data, and every formula is on one sheet with a worked example.

The lesson content is also published as static JSON (no key needed). Free to use with a link to monte.markets. Updated 2026-10-24.

## Start here

- [Home](https://monte.markets/): what the site is and where to begin
- [Study](https://monte.markets/study/): learn, practice and solve, with progress kept in the browser
- [All topics](https://monte.markets/study/learn/): the fourteen topics in teaching order
- [Formula sheet](https://monte.markets/study/learn/formulas/): every formula with a worked example
- [Glossary](https://monte.markets/study/learn/terms/): terms in plain words, each with an example
- [Play](https://monte.markets/play/): games that each hide one statistics idea
- [Why statistics](https://monte.markets/story/): the case for learning it
- [How it's built](https://monte.markets/built/): the stack, the data sources and the math

## Topics

- [Data and sampling](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/data/): Statistics is using data to make a decision. You rarely get to check everyone, so you check a slice (a sample) and use it to say something about the whole group (the population).
- [Where is the middle](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/center/): Mean is the average. Median is the middle once sorted. Mode is the most common.
- [How spread out is it](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/spread/): Range is the biggest value minus the smallest. Standard deviation is how far a typical value sits from the average.
- [Probability rules](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/prob/): List everything that can happen. Or means add and subtract the overlap.
- [Random variables and expected value](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/rv/): A random variable is a number whose value depends on chance.
- [Two variables: covariance, correlation, portfolios](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/two/): Covariance asks whether two things move together. Correlation is covariance scaled to run from −1 to +1.
- [Counting and the binomial](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/count/): When you repeat a yes-or-no trial n times with the same chance p each time, the number of yeses is binomial.
- [Poisson: counts per unit](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/poisson/): Poisson counts how many events land in a fixed window (a minute, an hour, a page) when they arrive at a steady average rate λ.
- [The normal curve and z](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/normal/): The normal is the bell. Any normal becomes the standard one by measuring in SDs from the mean: z = (y − μ) / σ.
- [Sampling distributions and the CLT](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/clt/): Take a sample and compute its mean. Take another and compute again.
- [Confidence intervals and sample size](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/ci/): A point estimate is one number. A confidence interval is that number plus and minus a margin: estimate ± critical value × standard error.
- [Hypothesis tests](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/test/): A hypothesis test asks one question: would this sample be surprising if nothing were going on?
- [Simple regression](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/reg/): Regression fits the straight line that makes the squared vertical misses as small as possible.
- [Multiple regression](https://monte.markets/study/learn/topics/mreg/): The same idea with several x's: fit a plane instead of a line.

## Open data

- [index.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/index.json): the list of endpoints, the license and the date
- [topics.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/topics.json): every topic with its idea, why it matters, formulas, hook, trap and URL
- [formulas.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/formulas.json): the formula sheet by topic, with worked examples
- [terms.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/terms.json): the glossary
- [sources.json](https://monte.markets/api/v1/sources.json): recommended free courses, books and videos
